course_name_original: CONTROLLO DELLE VIBRAZIONI E DEL RUMORE

learning_outcomes.text: The course provides the basic skills necessary for monitoring and remediation of vibrations and noise in environmental and industrial fields in accordance with current legislation.
Understanding of the physical concepts related to the control of vibrations and noise in environmental and industrial fields. Knowledge of the terminology used in this subject.
Being able to analyze and solve practical problems concerning the measurement and control of vibroacoustic phenomena.
Being able to identify the most appropriate methods to characterize and solve vibroacoustic problems.
Being able to present the topics covered during the course with appropriate technical language.
Being able to apply the acquired knowledge to applications different from those presented during the course, and to deepen the topics covered using literature different from that proposed.
Being able to identify the most appropriate methods for the analysis and remediation of vibroacoustic problems.
Being able to describe clearly and concisely, with appropriate language, the objectives, procedure, and results of the developed topics.
Being able to apply the acquired knowledge to different contexts from those presented during the course, and to deepen the topics covered using materials other than those proposed.

syllabus_topics: MECHANICAL VIBRATIONS
PERIODIC MOTION AND HARMONIC MOTION: VECTOR REPRESENTATION OF A HARMONIC MOTION
HARMONIC ANALYSIS
FUNDAMENTAL VIBRATORY PHENOMENA: MATHEMATICAL MODELS OF DISCRETE SYSTEMS
SYSTEMS WITH ONE AND 2-N GDL: FREE VIBRATIONS AND HARMONIC FORCED VIBRATIONS (RESONANCES), MATRIX APPROACH
METHODS FOR EXPERIMENTAL DETERMINATION OF DAMPING
VIBRATION ISOLATION TECHNIQUES
VIBRATION MEASUREMENT: SETUP OF THE MEASUREMENT CHAIN; PIEZOELECTRIC ACCELEROMETERS; LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS
ANALYSIS AND CONTROL OF VIBRATIONS IN WORK ENVIRONMENTS
LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS
NOISE MEASUREMENT
SOUND AND SOUND LEVELS: PROPERTIES OF SOUND; PROPERTIES OF SOUND WAVES; ACOUSTIC PARAMETERS; FREQUENCY WEIGHTING CURVES; SOUND PROPAGATION OUTDOORS; TRAFFIC NOISE
CURRENT LEGISLATION ON NOISE POLLUTION
MEASUREMENT CHAIN, MICROPHONES: CLASSIFICATION AND PRINCIPLE OF OPERATION
SOUND LEVEL METER: CALIBRATION AND OPERATION
NOISE MEASUREMENT METHODS
FREQUENCY ANALYSIS
INTERPRETATION OF RESULTS AND POST-PROCESSING SOFTWARE
BASICS OF STATISTICAL DATA ANALYSIS
FIELD EXERCISES
ANALYSIS AND CONTROL OF NOISE IN WORK ENVIRONMENTS

LABORATORY EXPERIENCES ON NOISE MEASUREMENT: SETUP AND CALIBRATION OF THE SOUND LEVEL METER CHAIN, SELECTION OF APPROPRIATE ACOUSTIC PARAMETERS, EXECUTION OF MEASUREMENTS, POST-PROCESSING, CREATION OF THE RESULTS REPORT
assessment_rules: The evaluation of the achievement of the set objectives will take place through an oral interview. To pass the exam, the student must demonstrate knowledge of vibration and noise monitoring and remediation techniques discussed during the course, as well as the theoretical bases for the study of mechanical vibrations and acoustic propagation. The evaluation will be expressed out of thirty. The final evaluation is obtained as the average of the partial evaluations on the individual oral questions. A minimum score of 18 is awarded for fragmentary knowledge and modest application capacity, while a maximum of 30 is awarded for complete and in-depth knowledge and significant application ability within a correct theoretical interpretation. Honors are awarded when the candidate demonstrates significant mastery, notable language proficiency, and autonomous processing capability, even in contexts different from those proposed by the teacher.
